abstract_summary: Deep research agents gather information from multiple sources and synthesize it into reports on complex, open-ended questions. Existing benchmarks assess report quality along several dimensions, but lack a dedicated knowledge-centric evaluation of which research directions a report covers and how deeply it explores...

A reference space for knowledge coverage needs to connect research topics with supporting evidence. Wikipedia
provides linked entities whose relationships can be examined in their source context. To span diverse domains,
we adopt all 24 topic categories from WebOrganizer (Wettig et al., 2025) and select two root entities per
category. Each root has a sufficiently detailed, reliably parseable article and enough outgoing links to support
expansion.
Starting from each root, we expand Wikipedia links breadth-first. Nodes represent entities, and edges
represent relationships supported by link anchors and surrounding text. We organize the retained expansion
as a rooted tree, with one parent per non-root node and a unique path from the root. This structure gives
each relation an identifiable position for subsequent rubric construction and coverage aggregation. Distance
from the root is

evidence.excerpt:
A full knowledge tree spans more material than a single research request can reasonably target. We therefore
sample smaller subgraphs, each defining the scope of one research case. A branch consists of one child of the
root and all its descendants: it represents a research direction, while paths within it capture chains of related
knowledge. Each case retains the root and 10 complete branches, preserving the knowledge structure within
the selected directions.
To make each scope coherent, Claude Opus 4.8 jointly selects three groups of branches from each tree, using
the candidate entities' page summaries, relations to the root, and descendant information. Branches within
a group are selected to provide complementary perspectives on a common research task; the three groups
do not share root branches. Retaining complete branches preserves the deeper relations needed to evaluate
coverage

The research request and its evaluation criteria should refer to the same knowledge scope. We therefore
use Claude Opus 4.8 to generate both the query and the rubrics from each sampled subgraph. For query
generation, the model receives the root entity and the sampled knowledge scope, and is instructed to frame
a natural research request around their broader themes. The prompt discourages listing hidden entities or
restating the subgraph as a checklist, so the agent is asked to investigate a topic rather than reproduce an
explicit answer outline.
To make the expected coverage traceable to evidence, we create one rubric per retained relation edge. Each
rubric asks whether the report covers the relationship between its source and target entities. The generator

Counting satisfied rubrics alone can give similar scores to reports with different coverage patterns. We
therefore retain the reference tree when aggregating judgments, distinguishing coverage across research
directions from coverage along related knowledge chains. An LLM judge assigns each hidden rubric one
of three verdicts:Satisfied,Partially Satisfied, orNot Satisfied. For coverage metric computation, we map
Satisfiedto1(covered) and bothPartially SatisfiedandNot Satisfiedto0(uncovered). These binary values
are then aggregated over the reference tree.
Breadth.Breadth measures how comprehensively a report covers the selected research directions. We give
these directions equal weight so that a branch with more rubrics does not dominate the score. Within a
branch, deeper relations can demonstrate coverage of a direction even when a shallower relation is missing.

three criteria: research value, public answerability, and alignment with their assigned domains (Table 3). All

research scopes that are not necessarily confined to a single domain; the queries nevertheless remain coherent,
publicly answerable, and sufficiently aligned with their assigned domains for benchmark evaluation.

missing_information: No reproducible review or selection methodology was detected.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Blinded human annotations on 3,695 rubric verdicts (Cohen's kappa 0.841; judge Macro-F1 0.893) and independent expert ratings of 72 reports (Kendall tau 0.696-0.751, Spearman rho 0.777-0.833) corroborate the automated judge's scores.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Topology-aware breadth, depth, and overall coverage computed from binary rubric verdicts assigned by the LLM judge Gemini 2.5 Pro.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: No system is trained or tuned against the benchmark; evaluated agents are off-the-shelf products, native-search models, and fixed backbone LLMs under a standardized local framework.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported claims regarding agent breadth-depth trade-offs, stability under metric perturbations, and alignment with human assessments are supported by detailed quantitative data and ablation experiments across multiple settings.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The benchmark evaluates 16 diverse deep research systems, native search models, and local-framework backbones. Extensive validation includes human expert consistency studies showing strong correlation with the topology-aware metrics, inter-annotator agreement (Cohen's kappa 0.841), rubric-level judge alignment (Macro-F1 0.893), and construction-model sensitivity tests.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Blinded independent evaluations by 10 PhD-level human annotators across 3,695 rubric verdicts (Cohen's kappa 0.841, Macro-F1 0.893) and 72 report-level expert quality assessments (Kendall tau 0.70-0.75, Spearman rho 0.78-0.83).
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Topology-aware breadth, depth, and overall coverage scores computed from binary rubric verdicts assigned by an automated LLM judge (Gemini 2.5 Pro).
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: None directly trained; systems evaluated are off-the-shelf agents and fixed backbone models executing standardized local or native retrieval pipelines.

primary.limitations: The evaluation relies on Wikipedia-derived knowledge structures which may favor certain entity types, and automated judge scoring requires careful thresholding, though validated extensively against human annotations.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology constructs multi-hop local knowledge trees from Wikipedia, samples branch-coherent subgraphs, and generates research queries and edge-grounded rubrics while controlling for lexical leakage. Aggregation recursively incorporates child coverage and continuity rewards, backed by comprehensive formal definitions and hyperparameter sensitivity analyses.
primary.quality_rationale: The study presents a rigorously formulated and thoroughly validated benchmark contribution with substantial scope, clear mathematical definitions, and extensive human-grounded calibration. The experimental controls and evaluations are exemplary.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces DRBench Pro, a knowledge-centric benchmark for deep research agents comprising 144 cases across 24 domains and 44,102 Wikipedia-grounded rubrics. It formalizes topology-aware metrics to evaluate coverage breadth across distinct research directions and depth along related knowledge chains.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The study presents a rigorously formulated and thoroughly validated benchmark contribution with substantial scope, clear mathematical definitions, and extensive human-grounded calibration. The experimental controls and evaluations are exemplary.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The evaluation relies on Wikipedia-derived knowledge structures which may favor certain entity types, and automated judge scoring requires careful thresholding, though validated extensively against human annotations.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
